headline: Visayas Grid Placed Under Red and Yellow Alerts as Power Reserves Tighten
seoTitle: Visayas Grid Under Red, Yellow Alerts September 16 | FMB News
seoDescription: NGCP placed the Visayas grid under red and yellow alerts on September 16 as forced outages and tight reserves constrained available power supply.
deck: NGCP scheduled a red alert for the Visayas grid from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m., with yellow-alert periods around it, as generating capacity and reserves remain tight.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The National Grid Corporation of the Philippines placed the Visayas grid under red and yellow alert status for Wednesday afternoon and evening as available power reserves remained tight.

GMA News, citing NGCP's advisory, reported a red alert from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. and yellow alerts from 4 p.m. to 5 p.m. and 6 p.m. to 8 p.m. Philippine News Agency separately reported continued tight supply linked to generating-unit outages.

sections.heading: What the alerts mean
paragraphs: NGCP defines a yellow alert as a period when the operating margin is insufficient to meet the grid's contingency requirement. A red alert means power supply is insufficient to meet consumer demand and the grid's contingency requirement.
An alert does not by itself mean every customer will lose electricity. Actual interruptions depend on system conditions and instructions implemented by distribution utilities.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The Visayas grid has faced repeated reserve pressure from unavailable generating capacity. PNA reported that generating units at major coal-fired plants remained in forced outage, contributing to the continued alert conditions.
NGCP operates the national transmission network. Its Visayas grid connects Cebu, Negros, Panay, Leyte, Samar and Bohol.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: A red alert indicates that the grid has little room to absorb additional generation losses or demand spikes. Consumers and businesses in the Visayas should monitor advisories from NGCP and their local distribution utilities during the affected hours.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for changes to the alert schedule, restoration of unavailable generating units, updated available-capacity and demand figures, and any rotational interruption advisories from distribution utilities.

verificationNotes: GMA News reported the September 16 alert schedule at 11:03 a.m. PHT, citing NGCP.
PNA independently reported the tight Visayas power-supply condition and forced generating-unit outages.
NGCP's official operations page confirms its role and definitions/context for grid operations.
The article does not claim that a red alert automatically means a blackout.
The hero is a genuinely relevant Philippine transmission-line file photograph licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 and is explicitly labeled contextual.
